title: Wallis/Stirling Asymptotics of Off-Diagonal Beta Values B(an+1, bn+1)

problemStatement.formal: Fix integers $a \ge b \ge 1$ with $a \ne b$, and let $H(a,b) = (a+b)\log(a+b) - a\log a - b\log b$. Then, as $n \to \infty$, $B(an+1,\,bn+1) = \dfrac{(an)!\,(bn)!}{((a+b)n+1)!} \sim \dfrac{1}{(a+b)n}\sqrt{\dfrac{2\pi\,ab}{(a+b)\,n}}\;e^{-H(a,b)\,n}$ in the sense of \texttt{Asymptotics.IsEquivalent}, generalizing the diagonal case $a=b=1$ (where $H(1,1)=2\log 2$ and $e^{-H(1,1)n}=4^{-n}$) proved in the parent entry.
problemStatement.plain: The parent gallery entry proves that the diagonal Euler Beta value B(n+1,n+1) decays like sqrt(pi n)/((2n+1) 4^n), extracted from Stirling's formula via a clean 'Wallis ratio' collapse. This problem asks whether the off-diagonal values B(an+1, bn+1) with a != b (for example B(2n+1, n+1)) admit the same treatment. Since B(an+1,bn+1) = (an)!(bn)!/((a+b)n+1)! is again a pure ratio of factorials, feeding each factorial through Mathlib's Stirling equivalence should yield a single asymptotic with an exponential rate governed by the binary entropy H(a,b) instead of the constant 4, together with an n^(-3/2) polynomial prefactor whose constant depends on a and b.
whyMatters: Off-diagonal Beta asymptotics are the analytic core of Laplace/saddle-point large-deviation estimates for the binomial: the exponential decay rate is exactly the binary relative entropy H(a,b), linking the entry to de Moivre-Laplace and Sanov-type results.

A Lean-verified general asymptotic would show the parent's Wallis-ratio method is a reusable template rather than a diagonal coincidence, and would supply an IsEquivalent entropy-rate decay lemma for general Beta values that Mathlib currently lacks.

knownResults: Parent entry beta-central-binomial-asymptotic: diagonal case a=b=1 gives C(2n,n) ~ 4^n/sqrt(pi n) and B(n+1,n+1) ~ sqrt(pi n)/((2n+1) 4^n), 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
Mathlib Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling: n! ~ sqrt(2 pi n)(n/e)^n, the sole analytic input.
Classical Laplace/saddle-point analysis gives B(an+1,bn+1) asymptotic to e^{-H(a,b)n} with H the binary relative entropy, but Mathlib states no such IsEquivalent result.
references: W. Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Vol. 1 (1968) - de Moivre-Laplace and Stirling-based binomial asymptotics.
N. G. de Bruijn, Asymptotic Methods in Analysis (1958) - Laplace/saddle-point derivation of Beta and factorial-ratio asymptotics.
DLMF section 5.11 (https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11) - asymptotic expansions of ratios of Gamma functions with large arguments.
